correctness.rationale: Every length-three word has a shadow of size one, two or three; constant and two-shadow codewords consume diagonal pair capacity, giving 3|C|<=2q²+3q. Each Steiner block contributes two of each directed off-diagonal pair via two reverse pairs; replacing abc by aab, bbc, acc preserves the off-diagonal incidence and consumes one extra diagonal for each of three disjoint symbols. Kirkman triple systems exist for q=3 mod6; factor-critical Steiner systems exist for q=1 mod6 with q>=13; an explicit q=7 certificate is checked. Standalone reproducibility confirms q=3,7,9,13 and all shadow types at q<=9. Only the imported infinite design theorems are non-elementary.

value.rationale: Solves a natural error-correction capacity at the shortest nontrivial deletion block length for two infinite congruence families, with a sharp universal shadow inequality and a constructive connection to resolvable and factor-critical Steiner systems. The exceptional q=7 has a finite certificate where the matching construction does not apply. The exact alphabet-dependent code sizes serve as reproducible benchmarks and show how repeated-letter shadows improve a directed-triple packing.
